name_note: The name is recent: the species was published as Butyrivibrio crossotus and reclassified as Eshraghiella crossota, so most literature uses the older name.

sentences.text: Eshraghiella crossota is the name proposed when Butyrivibrio crossotus was reclassified into a new genus within the family Lachnospiraceae.

The reclassification rests on analysis of 16S rRNA, groEL, recA and rpoB genes and genome sequences, with DNA-DNA hybridization and nucleotide identity values below the species thresholds for other Butyrivibrio species.
A cross-cohort analysis of type 2 diabetes reported Butyrivibrio crossotus depleted in individuals with the disease.
A nutrition intervention study reported an increased relative abundance of Eshraghiella crossota among species selected as potentially preventive against type 2 diabetes.
